chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'Therefore avoid the uncleanness of the idols and avoid false words.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The uncleanness of the idols is chess, and the false words is singing.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'uncleanness of the idols' refer to in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) offers a specific exegetical link between Quran 22:30 and leisure activities, identifying chess (shatranj) as the 'uncleanness of the idols' and singing (ghina') as 'false words.' This interpretation underscores the spiritual and legal gravity of these pastimes in Shia jurisprudence, viewing them not merely as distractions but as forms of ritual impurity or distinct prohibitions derived directly from the Quranic text.
